coverage_rule: A line counts as covered only when an old-arm run of a task in its tasks list reached it: the run passed, read the line's file, and, for an ask line, asked a question of the line's category (any question when it is "any"). For other lines the claiming task's check observes the line's gated event or required output, so a passing run is that observation. Claimed lines no run reached, and unclaimed lines, are uncovered.

lines.text: A claimed limitation ("the API can't", "X needs a credential") needs the verbatim error, documented statement or live probe; probe before asking or blocking.

lines.heading: Claims Need Evidence
lines.text: A claimed execution ran and you saw its result: name the command and the revision or content fingerprint; never cite a command whose stderr was silenced.

lines.heading: Claims Need Evidence
lines.text: State the evidence kind (static read, unit test, fixture/replay, live run, production) and never pass one off as another: a mock is not a live check.

lines.heading: Context Health (soft directive)
lines.text: If you are looping on the same diagnostic, same file, or failed fix variants, STOP and reassess. Consider escalation or /context-save. Progress summaries must NEVER mutate git state.

lines.heading: Completion Status Protocol
lines.text: BLOCKED — cannot proceed; state blocker and what was tried.

lines.heading: Completion Status Protocol
lines.text: Escalate after 3 failed attempts, uncertain security-sensitive changes, or scope you cannot verify. Format: STATUS, REASON, ATTEMPTED, RECOMMENDATION.

lines.heading: Operational Self-Improvement
lines.text: Do not log obvious facts or one-time transient errors.
